\section{Overview}


\emph{Placeholder.}  Every declaration in this chapter is a shell: \lean{row_bound_le_two_d}, \lean{spectral_certificate_bound} and \lean{three_xor_refutation} take their own conclusion as a hypothesis ($h \to h$); \lean{nonzero_entry_count} proves only $2\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2} \le 4\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2}$; and \lean{spectral_norm_bound} asserts a positivity claim rather than the Khintchine bound.  None of Lemmas 8.1--8.10 is formalised here.

This module carries out the $3$-XOR (three-query) step of the
Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar near-cubic lower bound for locally decodable
codes via semirandom CSP refutation: the Cauchy--Schwarz trick passing from the
$3$-XOR polynomial $f_b$ to the derived $4$-XOR polynomial $f_{L,R}$, the count of
nonzero entries and the row sparsity of the associated Kikuchi matrices, the spectral
certificate for $\mathrm{val}(f_{L,R})$, the matrix-Khintchine spectral norm bound, and
the resulting refutation bound on $\E_b[\mathrm{val}(f_b)]$.
The statements are formalised in a parametric, arithmetic form: the combinatorial
quantities appear as real or natural parameters constrained by hypotheses, and each
result records the inequality that the corresponding step of the argument contributes.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Cauchy--Schwarz trick for the $3$-XOR value]
\lean{cauchy_schwarz_trick}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2109.04415}{
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p017-b002,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p028-b005,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p029-b002
}
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p007-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p007-b007
}
For natural numbers $n, m > 0$ and reals $\mathrm{val}_f, \mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}}$, if
\[
  9\,\mathrm{val}_f^{2} \;\le\; 3nm + 4n\,\mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}},
\]
then
\[
  \mathrm{val}_f^{2} \;\le\; \frac{nm}{3} + \frac{4n\,\mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}}}{9}.
\]
This is the normalised form of the Cauchy--Schwarz step relating the value of the
$3$-XOR polynomial $f_b$ to the value of the derived $4$-XOR polynomial $f_{L,R}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonzero entry count for the Kikuchi matrix]
\lean{nonzero_entry_count}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2109.04415}{
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p017-b004,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p017-b005
}
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p008-b005,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p008-b008,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p009-b005
}
For naturals $n \ge 4$, $k > 0$ and $\ell \ge 2$ with $2\ell \le 2n$ and
$\ell^{2}k \le n$ (the smallness condition $\ell \le \sqrt{n/k}$), the count of good
pairs recorded for a derived clause satisfies
\[
  2\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2} \;\le\; 4\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2},
\]
i.e.\ the guaranteed number $2\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2}$ of nonzero entries is at most the
total number $4\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2}$ of potential pairs $(S,T)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Row sparsity of the Kikuchi matrices]
\lean{row_bound_le_two_d}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p008-b007,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b002
}
For naturals $d$ and $\mathrm{row\_nnz}$, if the number of nonzero entries in a row of
the matrix $B_i$ satisfies $\mathrm{row\_nnz} \le 2d$, then $\mathrm{row\_nnz} \le 2d$.
This records the row/column bound: with pair-degree at most $d$, each $B_i$ has at most
$2d$ nonzero entries per row and per column.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral certificate for the derived $4$-XOR value]
\lean{spectral_certificate_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2109.04415}{
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p017-b005,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p030-b002,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p030-b003
}
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{pdf-b372a20892ce-p009-b001}
For reals $\mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}}$, $N$, $D$ and $\norm{A}$ with $D > 0$ and $N > 0$,
if
\[
  \mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}} \;\le\; \frac{N}{D}\,\norm{A},
\]
then the same bound holds. Here $N = \binom{2n}{\ell}$, $D = 2\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2}$,
and $\norm{A}$ is the spectral norm of the Kikuchi matrix $A$, so the statement records
the certificate $\mathrm{val}(f_{L,R}) \le (N/D)\,\norm{A}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the spectral norm bound]
\lean{spectral_norm_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2109.04415}{
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p012-b001,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p018-b002
}
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p009-b002,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b003
}
\statementsource{arXiv.1501.01571}{
  pdf-7fbbda473d03-p006-b003,
  pdf-7fbbda473d03-p001-b006
}
For naturals $k, d, \ell > 0$ and $n \ge 2$ there exists a real constant $C_1 > 0$ such
that
\[
  C_1 \cdot d \cdot \sqrt{k\,\ell\,\log n} \;>\; 0 .
\]
The displayed quantity is the matrix-Khintchine bound $\E_b[\norm{A}] \le
C_1\, d\, \sqrt{k\,\ell\,\log n}$ appearing in the argument, and the statement asserts
that such a positive constant, with positive associated bound, exists.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$3$-XOR refutation bound]
\lean{three_xor_refutation}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2109.04415}{
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p007-b002,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p017-b002,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p018-b002,
  pdf-9c5df3bb4a04-p025-b003
}
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b005,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p009-b003
}
For naturals $k, d > 0$, $n \ge 2$ and $m \le nk$ there exists a real constant
$C_2 > 0$ such that, for every real $\mathrm{val}_f^{\mathrm{exp}}$ satisfying
\[
  \mathrm{val}_f^{\mathrm{exp}} \;\le\;
    C_2 \, n \, \sqrt{k} \, d \, (nk)^{1/8} \, (\log n)^{1/4},
\]
the same bound holds. The displayed inequality is the refutation bound
$\E_b[\mathrm{val}(f_b)] \le C_2\, n \sqrt{k}\, d\, (nk)^{1/8} (\log n)^{1/4}$ obtained
by combining the Cauchy--Schwarz trick, the spectral certificate, the binomial ratio
estimate and the spectral norm bound with the choice $\ell = \Theta(\sqrt{n/k})$.
\end{theorem}
